parameters.content:
## MCP client (Streamable HTTP)

One MCP session per call, N `tools/call` requests on it, parsed payloads back.

**Input items** — `{ label, tool, argsJson, mcpUrl }`. `label` is a free tag the caller reads back; `argsJson` is the tool arguments as a JSON string.
**Output items** — `{ label, tool, result }`, one per input item, in order.

Why four HTTP calls: MCP is stateful. `initialize` mints the session id (response header), `notifications/initialized` closes the handshake, `tools/call` does the work, `DELETE` frees the server-side session — a restricted MCP instance builds one server per session, so leaked sessions leak memory.

The handshake is retried (idempotent). **`tools/call` is not** — a tool call has side effects, and `send_telegram_message` replayed is a second message in the user's chat.

nodes.name: When called by another workflow
nodes.notes: One item per tool call: label (free-form tag the caller reads back), tool, argsJson (JSON string), mcpUrl.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "initialize", params: { protocolVersion: "2025-06-18", capabilities: {}, clientInfo: { name: "n8n", version: "1.0.0" } } }) }}

nodes.name: Open MCP session
nodes.notes: Streamable-HTTP handshake. The session id comes back as the mcp-session-id response header.

nodes.name: Finish the handshake
nodes.notes: Spec-mandated notification that closes the handshake. Answered 202 with an empty body.

nodes.name: Build one request per call
nodes.notes: Back to N items — one JSON-RPC tools/call body per requested tool, all on the one session.

nodes.name: Call the tools
nodes.notes: One request per item. No retry — tool calls have side effects and must not be replayed.

nodes.name: Parse the responses
nodes.notes: SSE → JSON-RPC → tool payload, with the caller's label put back on each item.

nodes.name: Close MCP session
nodes.notes: Frees the server-side session. A restricted MCP instance builds one server per session, so leaking sessions leaks memory. Failure here must not fail the run.

nodes.name: Return results to the caller
nodes.notes: Sub-workflow output: one item per call — { label, tool, result }.
